title: Automated Legal Document Summarization Pipeline
business: A mid-sized boutique law firm managing high volumes of discovery documents.
problem: The firm struggles with inconsistent manual summarization of lengthy legal filings, leading to delayed case preparation and high operational overhead for junior associates.
solution: The firm implements a structured inference pipeline using Fireworks AI to process legal documents. By utilizing the platform's support for structured outputs and high-throughput inference, the firm automates the extraction of key case facts into standardized JSON formats, ensuring consistency across all processed filings.
steps: Select a high-performance open-source model optimized for long-context reasoning via the Fireworks AI model catalog.
Configure the inference request to enforce structured JSON output, ensuring the model adheres to the firm's specific schema for case metadata.
Deploy the model to a dedicated GPU instance to ensure consistent latency during peak discovery periods.
Integrate the Fireworks API into the firm's internal document management system to trigger automated summarization upon file upload.
outcome: Legal teams receive standardized, machine-readable summaries immediately upon document ingestion, allowing associates to focus on high-level legal strategy rather than rote data entry.
limitation: The primary trade-off involves model context window constraints; if a document exceeds the maximum token limit of the chosen model, the summary may be incomplete. This can be checked by monitoring the response metadata for truncation flags or verifying input length against the model's documented context window.

code.content:
import fireworks.client

# Configure the client with the model and structured output requirements
response = fireworks.client.ChatCompletion.create(
  model="accounts/fireworks/models/llama-v3-70b-instruct",
  messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Summarize this legal filing: ..."}],
  response_format={"type": "json_object"} # Enforce JSON structure for downstream parsing
)
